title: Swap a kitchen counter receptacle for a GFCI

steps.text: Turn the breaker for this outlet off, then tell me when it's off.
steps.shortText: Breaker off. Tell me when it's off.
steps.reason: Everything after this is hands-on, so the circuit has to be off first.

check.question: Did the worker say the breaker is off?
check.prompt: Tell me when the breaker is off.

steps.text: Hold your tester on the receptacle where I can see it, and tell me what it reads.
steps.shortText: Test it dead and tell me the reading.
steps.reason: A breaker label can be wrong. The tester is the only proof the circuit is dead.

check.question: Did the worker say the tester shows no voltage?
check.prompt: Tell me what the tester reads.

steps.text: Take off the faceplate and pull the old receptacle out of the box so the wires are visible.
steps.reason: You need to see which wires come in from the panel before you land them on the new device.

check.question: Is the old receptacle pulled out of the box with its wires visible?
check.expect: A receptacle pulled forward out of a wall box, wires visible behind it.

steps.text: Turn the new GFCI around and find the LINE pair and the LOAD pair on the back. Show me the back.
steps.reason: A GFCI only protects correctly when the incoming power is on LINE.

check.question: Is the back of a GFCI receptacle with LINE and LOAD markings in frame?
check.expect: The back of a GFCI, LINE and LOAD terminal labels readable.

steps.text: Land the incoming wires on the LINE pair: hot on brass, neutral on silver. Leave LOAD empty.
steps.reason: Wires on LOAD leave the outlet unprotected even though it looks like it works.

check.question: Are the wires landed on the LINE terminals and not on the LOAD terminals?
check.expect: Both wires on the terminal pair marked LINE; LOAD terminals empty or taped.

steps.text: Mount the GFCI, put the faceplate on, turn the breaker back on, then press TEST and RESET. Tell me if it trips and resets.
steps.shortText: Mount it, power on, TEST then RESET. Tell me if it trips and resets.
steps.reason: TEST and RESET show the device trips the way it should.

check.question: Did the worker say it tripped on TEST and reset on RESET?
check.prompt: Did it trip on TEST and come back on RESET?
